stories.headline: VAT amendment bill proposes 15-day VAT return deadline
stories.summary: Parliament introduced Bill No. 114/2026 on 16 November to amend Section 64 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012. It proposes filing within 15 days after each tax period for most registered or registrable persons. Government bodies, autonomous bodies, banks, insurers and zero-return filers would have up to 20 days. If day 15 is a public holiday, filing moves to the next working day. The explanatory statement argues quarterly filing caused revenue and administrative difficulties; this is the government's stated rationale, not independently measured impact. Enactment was not verified at the research cut-off.
stories.why_it_matters: Distinguish a bill from an enacted law and remember the proposed VAT filing deadlines.
stories.exam_facts: Bill No. 114/2026; Section 64; ordinary proposed deadline 15 days; specified categories up to 20 days; related Ordinance No. 38 of 2026 issued 14 October 2026.
stories.exam_relevance: BCS: taxation, public finance and legislative procedure.

stories.headline: Kishoreganj-3 seat declared vacant after MP resignation
stories.summary: A 17 November extraordinary Gazette says seat No. 164, Kishoreganj-3, became vacant from 15 November 2026 after Dr Muhammad Osman Faruk resigned. It cites Article 67(2): a member's written resignation takes effect when received by the Speaker, or by the Deputy Speaker in specified circumstances. Article 123(4) provides an ordinary 90-day period to fill a vacancy not caused by dissolution of Parliament, subject to its proviso.
stories.why_it_matters: The vacancy date and Gazette publication date differ. Articles 67(2) and 123(4) are key constitutional provisions.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank accepts Tk 6,500 crore in Treasury bills
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank's auction table lists 91-day, 182-day and 364-day Treasury bills issued on 16 November 2026. Accepted face value totalled Tk 6,500 crore: Tk 3,000 crore, Tk 2,500 crore and Tk 1,000 crore respectively. Cut-off yields were 8.0884%, 8.2699% and 8.3900%. The three official sale values sum to Tk 6,266.36 crore. Treasury bills are short-term government securities issued at a discount and redeemed at face value.

stories.headline: COP31 highlights climate transparency reporting
stories.summary: COP31's high-level segment resumed in Antalya, Türkiye, on 17 November. The UNFCCC schedule listed a ministerial dialogue on transparency from 13:00 to 15:00. A synthesis update discussed the first 137 Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs) and said 61 Parties, representing about 66% of 2020 global greenhouse-gas emissions, had reported progress against their nationally determined contributions. The Enhanced Transparency Framework informs the Global Stocktake. Reporting progress does not mean every country has achieved its targets.
stories.why_it_matters: BTR, NDC and Global Stocktake are recurring climate-diplomacy and international-affairs concepts.
